txt: Her brown eyes linger on you for a moment.
She doesn't reply, but her eyes are still sad.
She just looks at you and says nothing.
She merely nods in response.
She nods in agreement.
She sighs and looks at you with something akin to compassion in her eyes. "Can we help you with something?"
The woman has a slight smirk on her face.
The woman in an RCM patrol officer's uniform winces as she notices you.
"Actually never mind. Don't tell me about it. It will just turn into another..." She stops mid-sentence.
"By the...?" She pinches the root of her nose.
"C'mon, Jean..." The woman next to him sighs. "It looks like it's been a rough week on him."
"C'mon, Jean..."
"C'mon, stop it," she says quietly.
"Calm down," she says to the man, then turns to you.
"Can I actually help you with something?" She looks at you apologetically.
"Do you now?" she asks, narrowing her eyes. After a moment she shakes her head.
"God, everybody knows your name..." She waves at you in a discarding motion. "Please go finish your investigation, so everyone can go home."
"Honestly..." Her sad eyes scan your face, looking for signs of deceit. "I don't care. I don't think anyone does anymore."
"I don't know..." She's still avoiding your gaze. "I mean, why would I want to talk to you?"
"I don't understand what this conversation is about anymore." She's trying to look elsewhere.
"I don't..." She looks around. "I don't know what to say."
"I just want to do my job, that's all," she says quietly and looks away.
"I know."
"I would really prefer not to talk to you right now..."
"I'm definitely not the cavalry."
"I'm just looking out for..."
"It was very nice. Different, but good kind of different. I liked it."
"Jean, detective." She looks at both of you. "I don't understand what you're talking about."
"Jean, he said okay, give it a rest."
"Jean, he's obviously suffering..." The woman stops mid-sentence.
"Jean," she quietly interjects, giving you a compassionate side glance. "He's not right... treat him like you'd treat McCoy's little brother."
"Jean..." she quietly interjects, giving you a compassionate side glance. "He's not right, don't make it worse and... and *I* really liked it."
"Like undercover?" The woman in the RCM uniform interjects.
"No you're not, you're not the only cop in the world." She shakes her head and breathes out.
"No, Harry, neither of us are firefighters," she says with a heavy sigh, and falls silent.
"No, it's okay." She raises her eyes to meet your gaze. "I am not. Polite. I'm just tired... was there something else you wanted?"
"No, no I don't." It doesn't look like she does -- the *police* uniform she's wearing is a dead giveaway.
"No, you haven't wronged me. It's okay." She shakes her head and breathes out.
"No." She sighs. "Okay. Sort of. But not with you. Like you are now. Don't take this the wrong way..."
"Of course I'm *with him*..." She seems startled by her own tone. "Why do you ask?"
"Okay, fine. Let's talk. What did you want?"
"Okay..."
"Okay." It looks like she's about to add something, but then she changes her mind.
"Please," she looks at you, then him, then you again. "Let's not turn this into another *exchange*, okay?"
"Stop it, Jean..." she says quietly and turns to you. "No, he has never been a firefighter. No one here is a firefighter."
"That... that was pretty good, Harry." She pokes her companion with an elbow. "Wasn't it Jean?"
"The sooner you figure this hanging out, the sooner everyone can go home."
"This isn't helping," she says, shaking her head and looking at the man with sunglasses disapprovingly.
"Uh... okay. Yes, that was pretty good."
"Uh.... okay." Her tone doesn't suggest she's convinced.
"Uh..." she seems confused for a moment. "It means I'm a patrol officer, sir."
"Well, I... uh..." She looks extremely uncomfortable right now. "I guess I..."
"Well... raising two children and half a husband on a patrol officer's wage. Yes, I guess I am working class."
"What *Precinct*..." She just sighs.
"What? No. No, he's not... what are you talking about?"
"Word of the End to come..." She shakes her head, tired.
"Yes, I called you by your name, what about it?" She sounds slightly agitated and... sad.
"Yes, did you want something from me?"
"Yes," she looks at you. "What is it?"
"Yes..." Her voice is quiet. "A police woman who just wants to do her job, that's all," she says quietly and looks away.
"Yes." She nods. "I am."
"You can sometimes be a real asshole, you know that?" Surprisingly, the words don't seem to be directed at you.
"You do look..." She sighs. "It looks like it's been a tough week for him."
"You're a fucking asshole." She says this with quiet dignity. "Are we done here?"
